intro.name: Krish Vedak
intro.tagline: Thinking about how silicon turns ideas into computation.
bio: Hi, I'm Krish. I study computer architecture and VLSI design, and I'm curious about what happens between a line of code and the transistors that run it.
This site is my notebook: what I'm interested in, what I've learned, what I've built, and things I write to understand them better.

interests.title: Processor microarchitecture
interests.text: Pipelines, out-of-order execution, branch prediction and the trade-offs behind them.

interests.title: Digital VLSI design
interests.text: RTL to layout: synthesis, timing closure, and physical design flows.

interests.title: Memory systems
interests.text: Caches, coherence and bandwidth, where performance is often won or lost.

interests.title: Low-power design
interests.text: Making circuits efficient through clock gating, voltage scaling and smarter design choices.

interests.title: Hardware accelerators
interests.text: Domain-specific designs for machine learning and signal processing.

interests.title: Open-source hardware
interests.text: RISC-V and open EDA tools that make chip design more accessible.

items.name: Intro. to Classical and Quantum Physics

projects.title: Quantum Circuit StateVector ASIC
projects.context: Course project · EE671 VLSI Design · Prof. Laxmeesha Somappa
points: Designed a parameterizable quantum state-vector ASIC in Verilog RTL, supporting 4, 5 and 6 qubits with six gate operations (H, X, Z, T, CNOT and multi-controlled Z) on 16-bit Q2.14 fixed-point amplitudes.
Developed a multi-lane architecture with configurable pipeline depth and 1, 2, 4 and 8 parallel lanes, backed by an exact cycle model verified on all 32 recorded runs.

Verified the RTL bit-exactly against a Python model with Grover's search, taking it through RTL-to-layout implementation: 12 synthesis runs (met 5 ns, 200 MHz) and two layouts that closed timing at 125 MHz.
Designed the controller FSM (IDLE, ISSUE, WAIT, DONE) with a drain after every batch, and derived the exact cycle model that matched all 32 recorded runs.

Wrote the micro-architecture specification: the 32-bit instruction format, the ready/done handshake, the lane organization and the 2L-port state array, which fixed the interfaces between the RTL blocks.

Defined the numerical design: Q2.14 arithmetic with 18-bit and 34-bit intermediates, round-half-up and saturation, and showed that the quantized 1/√2 constant explains about 95% of the observed norm drift.

projects.title: Prefetcher and Cache Replacement Design
projects.context: Course project · CS683 Advanced Computer Architecture · Prof. Biswabandan Panda
points: Built an L1D Stride Pattern Prefetcher that detects repeating non-uniform strides, reaching 1.020/1.017/1.037 speedup vs 1.005/1.000/1.002 for IP-stride, and raising miss coverage from 0.7–5.2% to 20.6–35.5%.
Designed an instruction-aware L2 replacement policy (I-RRIP) and a dynamic version using leader-set sampling, cutting L2 instruction MPKI by 13–51%, tested on ChampSim.
Combined SPP with a prefetch-aware dynamic I-RRIP using set dueling, giving the best IPC on all three traces (up to 1.047 speedup, +2.9% over SPP alone).

projects.title: WashU-2 16-bit CPU Architecture
projects.context: Course project · EE309 Microprocessors · Prof. V Rajbabu
points: Designed and implemented a 16-bit accumulator-based CPU (WashU-2) in VHDL, building a multi-cycle FSM with 17 states to control instruction fetch, decode and execute phases.
Implemented the core instruction set including arithmetic/logic operations (ADD, AND) and conditional branching (BRPOS), verified through waveform analysis and FSM state tracing.
Authored self-checking VHDL testbenches with automated pass/fail assertions to validate ALU correctness, memory read/write behavior and branch logic across multiple test cases.

projects.title: Device Driver Development for 8051 Microcontroller
projects.context: Course project · EE337 Microprocessors Lab · Prof. Miriyala Indu Vardhan
points: Designed and implemented a bare-metal I2C driver stack in embedded C, progressing from direct register manipulation to a fully realized hardware abstraction layer.
Integrated multiple I2C peripherals (BMP280 sensor, DS1307 RTC) with read/write support and protocol-level error handling via I2C status-register validation.
Delivered a unified telemetry system displaying calibrated sensor data on LCD and UART serial output, debugging real hardware timing constraints (power-up delays, signal integrity).

projects.title: Zigzag RLE Compression Engine for 8×8 Data Blocks
projects.context: Course project · EE214 Digital Circuits Lab · Prof. Mahesh Ashok Bhaganagare
points: Designed a zigzag-scan Run-Length Encoding (RLE) compressor/decompressor in VHDL for 8×8 data blocks, using FSM-driven control to traverse matrix data in JPEG-style diagonal order.
Built a standalone RLE encoder and decoder as independent modules, each handling variable-length run buffers and reconstructing the original matrix from compressed symbol-count pairs.
Developed an integrated top-level testbench that feeds test data through the full encode-decode pipeline and self-verifies correctness in hardware, driving pass/fail status flags.

projects.title: Verilog Coupled Differential Equation Numerical Solver
projects.context: Course project · EE224 Digital Systems · Prof. Debanjan Bhowmik
points: Designed a parallel hardware solver on a Field Programmable Gate Array to solve the MaxCut optimization problem by utilizing the Kuramoto model using Intel Quartus Prime Lite Software.
Implemented the core computational unit in Verilog, integrating a hardware-optimized sin() function (via CORDIC/LUT) and the Euler numerical method for efficient hardware synthesis.

Developed a comprehensive Verilog testbench to functionally verify the RTL design, validating the solver's final outputs against expected results for various graph instances (e.g., Mobius Ladder) up to 10 nodes.

projects.title: Semiconductor Process Design & Simulation
projects.context: Purdue University online project · Optimizing atomic-level fabrication recipes and CMOS process flows for high-yield manufacturing
points: Simulated Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD) using vfablab, tuning precursor pulse timing (0.1 s) and process temperature (110–140 °C) to achieve conformal, self-limiting High-K dielectric growth.
Ran wet/dry thermal oxidation recipes at 1000 °C, applying Deal-Grove kinetics to control oxide thickness while minimizing thermal shock and crystal defects.
Studied Moore's Law scaling limits near the 0.54 nm silicon lattice level and outlined process flows for depletion-mode NMOS, factoring in ion implantation dose and lithography constraints.

projects.title: Virtual Reality with Convolution
projects.context: Course project · EE229 Signal Processing 1 · Advisor: Prof. Preeti Rao
points: Coded a virtual reality audio system by applying discrete convolution to a dry audio source with Binaural Room Impulse Responses (BRIR), simulating immersive acoustic environments in Scilab and Python.
Implemented a discrete convolution algorithm from scratch and validated its accuracy against Python's np.convolve, achieving a maximum absolute error of 4.441 × 10⁻¹⁶.

Visualized the acoustic impact of convolution by isolating and plotting the pure “Room Sound” (reverberations) via waveform subtraction between the original and convolved audio signals, conducting amplitude analysis.
